summary.text: Sea salt is salt made by evaporating seawater, and it is also called bay salt or solar salt.
It is mostly sodium chloride, but commercial sea salts vary widely, with other salts making up from under 0.2% to 22% of the total.
Its nutritional value is about the same as table salt's, and it contains only small amounts of iodine.

facts.label: Ancient mention
facts.value: Vinaya Pitaka, Buddhist scripture, mid-5th century BC

facts.label: Where made today
facts.value: Mostly Mediterranean and other warm, dry climates

items.prompt: Rock salt is dug from mines deep underground, far from any coast. Where did that salt originally come from?

options.label: A shallow sea that dried up long ago
Rock melted deep inside the Earth

items.explain: All mined salts were once sea salts, usually from an evaporating shallow sea in the distant past.

items.prompt: A company wants to make sea salt without burning any fuel. Which kind of coast suits it best?
items.explain: In warm, dry climates the water can be evaporated by the sun alone, which is why modern production is mostly found there.

items.prompt: A shopper swaps table salt for sea salt, hoping it is more nutritious. What do they actually get?
items.explain: Sea salt and table salt are both mainly sodium chloride, so their nutritional value is about the same.

items.prompt: A jar sold in the US is labelled 'sea salt'. Can you be sure the salt came from the sea?

options.label: No, it only has to meet purity rules
Yes, the label is legally binding
No, it is always mined rock salt

items.explain: In the US, salt labelled 'sea salt' might not come from the sea, as long as it meets the FDA's purity requirements.

items.prompt: Some boutique salts from France come out a natural pinkish gray. What gives them that color?

options.label: Rust from the metal drying pans
Clays and algae in the local waters
Smoke from fires used to dry them
Extra iodine added at the factory

items.explain: The colors and flavors of sea salts come from local clays and algae in the waters where the salt is harvested.

items.prompt: A cook replaces iodised table salt with plain sea salt. Which nutrient might they now get less of?
items.explain: Iodised salt has iodine salts mixed in, while sea salt holds only small amounts of iodine.
